extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, grantees and contractors (care provider facilities), legal service providers, state/local licensing authorities, and public stakeholders commenting on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_short: ORR UC care and placement rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed HHS/ORR regulatory framework defining scope, standards, processes, and definitions governing the care, placement, release, services, oversight, and review procedures for unaccompanied children in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of this part
rubrics_metrics.description: This part governs aspects of placement, care, and services provided to unaccompanied children in Federal custody referred to the UC Program as authorized by 6 U.S.C. 279 and 8 U.S.C. 1232, and includes provisions implementing the Flores settlement agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions are separable and severable; if any provision is stayed or invalid, the remaining provisions continue in effect. ORR does not fund or operate facilities other than standard programs, restrictive placements (including secure facilities and heightened supervision facilities), or emergency/influx facilities, absent a specific waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions incorporated for regulatory application
rubrics_metrics.description: The part provides a comprehensive set of definitions (e.g., care provider facility, case file, case manager, best interest, home study, emergency, influx, etc.) that inform applicability and implementation of standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are authoritative for interpreting obligations throughout Part 410; many later regulatory duties and standards rely on these precise definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best interest standard and factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Best interest is the standard ORR applies in determining decisions and actions regarding a child's care; factors include child's expressed interests (age/maturity appropriate), mental and physical health, wishes of parents/legal guardians, intimacy of family relationships, child's adjustment to community, cultural background and primary language, stability/history of living environment, individualized needs including disabilities, and child's development and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is inexhaustive; ORR considers these factors 'as appropriate' when evaluating what is in a child's best interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider facility definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facility means any physical site housing unaccompanied children in ORR custody operated by an ORR-funded residential program, including shelters, group homes, individual family homes, residential treatment centers, secure or heightened supervision facilities, and emergency/influx facilities; excludes out-of-network facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines which facilities must comply with the Part's standards and which do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case file content and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Case file comprises physical/electronic records pertinent to care and placement: biographical info, birth/marriage certificates, ORR forms and attachments (e.g., photographs), incident reports, medical/dental records, mental health evaluations, case notes and educational records, immigration forms/papers, home studies/post-release service records, family reunification info including sponsor's personal/financial data, case disposition, correspondence, SSN, juvenile/criminal history records, and other relevant records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of unaccompanied children are the property of ORR whether in ORR or a grantee/contractor's possession; grantees/contractors may not release these records without prior ORR approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case manager responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Case manager coordinates assessments, individual service plans, and efforts to release children from ORR custody and ensures services are documented within each child's case file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case manager may coordinate these duties in whole or in part and is responsible for documentation and follow-through on placement and service plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical restraints definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical restraints include drugs administered to chemically restrain children and external chemicals such as pepper spray or other inflammatory/aerosol agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition clarifies what constitutes chemical restraint for purposes of any prohibitions or standards (see related behavior management and restraint provisions in the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical restraint definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical restraint means any device attached or adjacent to the child's body that the child cannot easily remove that restricts freedom of movement or normal access to the child's body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify prohibited or tightly regulated restraint practices under behavior management standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child advocates definition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Child advocates are third parties appointed by ORR consistent with TVPRA (8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(6)) who make independent recommendations regarding the best interests of an unaccompanied child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Child advocates provide independent input to inform placement and care decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and convincing evidence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear and convincing evidence means a standard of evidence requiring the factfinder be convinced that a contention is highly probable (substantially more likely true than untrue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines evidentiary threshold where this standard is specified elsewhere in rule (e.g., for certain findings or determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrective action means steps taken to correct any care provider facility noncompliance identified by ORR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames ORR enforcement and remediation options when grantees/contractors fail to meet standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and emergency incidents definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency: act/event (natural disaster, fire, civil disturbance, medical/public health concerns, etc.) preventing timely transport/placement or impacting conditions. Emergency incidents: urgent situations with immediate/severe threat to child safety/well-being requiring immediate action, including abuse/neglect with serious injury, death in custody (including out-of-network), medical emergencies, mental health emergencies requiring hospitalization, and unauthorized absences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers special contingency planning, response obligations, and possibly use of emergency/influx facilities not otherwise licensed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency or influx facility definition and licensing exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An emergency or influx facility opens temporarily during an influx or emergency to provide shelter/services; may not be licensed or may be exempted from licensing by State/local agencies; may be on federally-owned or leased property where state/local licensing may not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facilities are a distinct category from standard or secure facilities and are governed by special placement and minimum standards for emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency safety situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency safety situation: child presents a risk of imminent physical harm to self or others as demonstrated by overt acts or expressed threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition informs immediate safety interventions and permissible actions by staff consistent with behavior management rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOIR accredited representative recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: EOIR accredited representative is a representative of a qualified nonprofit or similar organization recognized by DOJ under 8 CFR part 1292; an EOIR accredited representative representing a child in ORR custody may file notice of representation to receive updates on the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how accredited representatives interact with ORR to obtain custody-related updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family planning services definition and abortion exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Family planning services include FDA-approved contraceptives (including emergency contraception), pregnancy testing and counseling, STI services, and referrals. The term 'family planning services' does not include abortions, which are addressed separately as medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what reproductive health services fall within routine planning services versus those requiring heightened ORR involvement and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Reunification Packet requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Family Reunification Packet is an application and supporting documentation a potential sponsor must complete to seek the release of an unaccompanied child; ORR uses this and other procedures to determine a sponsor's ability to provide for the child's physical and mental well‑being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms the basis for sponsor suitability assessment and home study initiation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightened supervision facility definition and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Heightened supervision facility is a licensed program that meets standard program standards (§410.1302) and is designed for children needing close supervision but not secure placement; provides 24‑hour custody/care/treatment, stricter security measures than a shelter (intensive staff supervision), may have a secure perimeter but not internal major restraining construction associated with juvenile detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates placement types and appropriate settings for children with higher supervision needs while avoiding classification as juvenile detention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home study definition and triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Home study: in‑depth investigation of a potential sponsor's ability to ensure a child's safety and well‑being, including living condition assessment, standard of care, interviews with sponsor/household members; conducted where required by TVPRA, this part, or at ORR's discretion including cases where child's safety/well‑being is in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home studies are required in statutorily mandated situations and may be used as a discretionary safeguard by ORR to evaluate sponsor suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influx definition (trigger for influx/contingency operations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Influx means net bed capacity of ORR's standard programs that is occupied or held for placement meets or exceeds 85 percent for seven consecutive days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative trigger determines when contingency/influx operations and emergency facility rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal guardian definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal guardian means an individual lawfully vested by a competent court with power and duty to care for/manage property, rights, and affairs of a child or incapacitated adult (foreign or domestic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine legal relationships and decision‑making authority for placement and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal service provider role and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal service provider means an organization or individual attorney providing legal services to unaccompanied children (pro bono or ORR funded), providing Know Your Rights presentations, screenings for relief, and/or direct legal representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to the greatest extent practicable that all unaccompanied children in ORR care have access to legal advice and representation in immigration proceedings; where pro bono counsel is impracticable and appropriations allow, ORR may fund legal service providers to provide direct representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical services requiring heightened involvement include (1) significant surgical/medical procedures, (2) abortions, and (3) medical services necessary to address threats to life or serious jeopardy to health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These services trigger heightened ORR oversight, consent procedures, and involvement distinct from routine healthcare services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC) instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: NOC is an instrument used by home study and post‑release services providers, ORR care providers, and the ORR National Call Center to document and notify ORR of certain concerns arising after a child is released from ORR custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a standardized mechanism for post‑release monitoring and reporting of sponsor concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Placement (NOP) requirement for restrictive placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Placement is a written notice provided to children placed in restrictive placements explaining reasons for placement; a copy is kept in the child's case file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and documentation when a child is placed in a restrictive setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards and required services subpart (§410.1300–§410.1311)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart D sets out purpose, applicability, minimum standards for standard programs, reporting/monitoring/quality control/recordkeeping standards, behavior management and prohibition on seclusion/restraint, staff training and case manager requirements, language access services, healthcare services, child advocates, legal services, psychotropic medications, and services for children with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated topics identify the substantive areas where ORR will prescribe minimum operational and service standards for care provider facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations and criteria for restrictive placement (§410.1103–410.1105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart B addresses the placement process after referral, types of care provider facilities, generally applicable placement considerations, placement in standard non‑restrictive programs, and criteria for placing a child in a restrictive placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the procedural and substantive criteria used to determine appropriate placement settings, including restrictive placements when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers, age determinations, and emergency/influx operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subparts G, H, and I set rules for transfers within ORR facility network, conducting age determinations and information used as evidence, and contingency planning/minimum and placement standards for emergency or influx facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies processes and evidentiary standards for movement of children, age assessment procedures and emergency operations planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of review of certain ORR decisions (restrictive placement reviews, placement review panel, risk determination hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart J establishes purpose and procedures for restrictive placement case reviews (§410.1901), Placement Review Panel (§410.1902), and risk determination hearings (§410.1903).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR proposes to establish a hearing process through an independent HHS adjudicator providing the same substantive protections as immigration court bond hearings under the FSA; responsibility for these hearings would shift from DOJ to HHS, requiring implementation resources and staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and scope of UC Office of the Ombuds
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart K would establish the UC Office of the Ombuds (§410.2000–410.2004), including scope/responsibilities, organization, confidentiality, and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR anticipates Ombuds would be a career civil servant with expertise in dispute resolution, oversight/regulatory matters, experience with unaccompanied children/child welfare, and knowledge of ORR policy/regulations; ORR estimated annual staffing costs and solicits comment on staffing and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR obligation to follow/coordinate with State/local licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where ORR enters cooperative agreements/contracts with facilities, ORR requires organizations administering facilities to abide by all applicable State or local licensing regulations and laws; ORR policies and proposed regulations are designed to complement—not supplant—State/local licensing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR intends to minimize conflicts with state law and to work within existing licensing frameworks; comments from state/local facility representatives are welcomed during rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable costs under grant awards (45 CFR 75.403–75.405)
rubrics_metrics.description: All care provider facility costs discussed are ORR grantee allowable costs under Basic Considerations for cost provisions at 45 CFR 75.403–75.405 insofar as costs are reasonable, necessary, ordinary, treated consistently, and allocable to the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional unbudgeted costs that cannot be absorbed may be allowable through requests for supplemental funds to cover remediation or compliance expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act compliance and OMB approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule does not create or change a collection of information; reporting requirements associated with current practices have been approved under PRA with specific OMB control numbers cited and expiration dates; one consent form is pending OMB approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR submitted required PRA materials to OMB and notes prior approvals for placement/service forms and other ORR forms; rulemaking does not trigger new PRA burdens beyond existing approved collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) and small entity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR considered effects on small entities (small businesses, non-profits, local governments <50,000 population) and preliminarily certifies the rule will not have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; ORR requests data from the public if they believe the rule would have significant impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR identifies current grantees as non‑profits likely to qualify as small entities and invites comments and alternatives to minimize economic impact where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) threshold assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR assessed whether the rule would trigger UMRA's expenditure threshold (current threshold $177 million updated); the proposed rule would not mandate requirements meeting or exceeding that threshold and does not create a Federal intergovernmental or private sector mandate because ORR's requirements are conditions of Federal assistance rather than binding mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMRA exclusions for conditions of Federal assistance apply; ORR explains rationale for no UMRA-covered mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would not have substantial direct effects on States or change distribution of power among levels of government; ORR designed policies and cooperative agreements to complement state/local licensing and minimize federalism conflicts; nonetheless ORR invites comments from state/local facility representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR determined a federalism summary impact statement is not required but will accept state/local input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule meets standards in EO 12988 sections 3(a) and 3(b)(2) to minimize litigation, eliminate ambiguity, and reduce burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule language was drafted with attention to clarity and reducing potential litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives consideration and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR considered alternatives including not promulgating regulations or expanding scope to other TVPRA areas (e.g., asylum proceedings) and rejected them on operational, legal, and policy grounds; rule is focused on care and placement consistent with ORR statutory authority and FSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document explains reasoning for choosing codification of ORR practices to provide uniform standards and public transparency; ORR may issue separate regulations later on other topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that grantees/contractors request supplemental funds for unbudgeted compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional costs associated with remedial actions necessary to meet promulgated requirements that were not budgeted and cannot be absorbed within existing budgets would be allowable for grantees to submit requests for supplemental funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR reiterates this is the mechanism for small entities and grantees to seek funding to implement newly codified requirements when costs are otherwise unbudgeted.
